exposure: within a week after vaginal delivery
cohort: A cohort of 12 women was followed during their first term pregnancy and after vaginal delivery.
finding: Anatomic changes measured by dynamic MRI and POP-Q examinations demonstrated significant pelvic floor descent at 3 months postpartum, but these changes did not significantly correlate with changes in symptoms.
mod_finding: The study focused on women who had a vaginal delivery, revealing increased bladder descent, POP stage, and genital hiatus at 3 months postpartum, while symptom scores generally returned to baseline levels.
